title: UI: the live mini-map, the web page and review pages
tagline: How a run is watched: a mini-map window, a phone page, recordings frame by frame
summary: The ui package only reads: it follows the telemetry the hunting commands and the perception service write, folds it into a State, and draws the map with what the stack sees, predicts and plans, in a tkinter window beside the game and on a web page pushed to a phone over Server-Sent Events (also reachable through a Cloudflare tunnel). The same server shows review pages (overlaid recordings, frame by frame, downloadable as video) built offline by tools/review_pages, and /tls/, a capture viewer that is not part of the player.
details_md:
**What the UI is for.** The autonomous player runs as separate processes (the elevated key player, the
perception service, a hunting command). The perception service and the hunting commands report what they see, plan and
do as *telemetry*: one JSON line per record, `{"t": seconds, "topic": ..., ...}`, appended to `gamelab/lab/telemetry/<time>-<command>.jsonl` (the
perception service to `<time>-perceive.jsonl`). The `ui` package is the only reader that turns this into something to
look at. It never sends keys and never touches the game; `tests/test_architecture.py` lets it import only
`localization`, `motion`, `attack` and the shared modules, and nothing in the stack imports it.

**The pipeline.**

```
telemetry files ──> source.poll() ──> State.apply ──┬─> MapView.draw ──> Tk window (MapWindow, every 100 ms)
 (hunt command,      LiveSource /                   │
  perception svc)    ReplaySource / planned          └─> web.Feed ──SSE──> phone page (canvas, its own copy of the drawing)
```

- **Sources** (`sources.py`) all answer `poll() -> (fresh, records)`. `LiveSource` follows the newest run as it grows
  (looking for a newer one at most once a second, going on into a run's next part), and while the perception service's
  file is growing (it gave records within the last 3 s) it takes what's on screen from there (`scene`, `tracks`, `exp`
  records and the `died`, `exp_gain`, `hp_drop`, `touch`, `touch_fix` events) and the rest (routes, chains, the hunt's
  rules, the log) from the command. `ReplaySource` plays a recording at its own pace; `planned` previews a route with no game.
- **State** (`state.py`) keeps the latest record of each kept topic, the tour, her last 240 positions and the log.
- **MapView** (`render.py`) is pure drawing with OpenCV: State in, RGB out, about 1 ms for the window's picture. It
  also exports the colours and geometry the web page uses, and draws the route coverage report.
- **MapWindow** (`app.py`) shows it in tkinter beside the game, never taking the focus (the player only presses keys
  while the game is in front, and screen captures see whatever is on top).
- **The web server** (`web.py`, standard library) runs in the same process when `python -m gamelab minimap` starts
  (port 8765; `web` or `--web-only` for the page alone). A Feed thread reads every 25 ms; each open page gets a
  Server-Sent Events stream: a snapshot, then the new records (coalesced), text changes at most 5 times a second, and a
  ping after 5 s with nothing to send. The page draws the map on a canvas at the phone's frame rate, her position interpolated 100 ms behind
  the run's clock. Pushing records instead of JPEGs took the page from 1.6 pictures a second, 280 ms old, 45-70 KB/s
  to ~20 ms latency at ~2 KB/s (measured on 2026-10-20 from the moment a record is in the file; since 2026-10-26 the
  telemetry recorder writes in batches `FLUSH_S` = 0.2 s apart, so a record can wait up to 0.2 s before it is there).

**Exposure.** Since 2026-10-24 the page asks for no key: the user serves it through a named Cloudflare tunnel
(cloudflared, configured outside the repo) and on the LAN; anyone who reaches it can watch and steer a replay. The one
exception is `/tls/`, which requires a Cloudflare Access login for requests that come through the tunnel.

**Review pages.** The same server serves `/review` (`review.py`): folders of frames with perception's outcome drawn on
them, stepped through one frame at a time on a phone, with smaller frames on request, preloading, and a Download video
button (`video.py` + `h264.ps1`: Windows' own H.264 encoder, then the MP4 index moved first so a phone can play it as
it arrives). The Lie Detector and Violetta review sets are built offline from the alarm clips by
`tools/review_pages/build.py`.

**Not the player.** `ui/tls/` is a viewer of a separate packet recorder's captures with their TLS decrypted, moved onto
this server on 2026-11-13 for its tunnel. It is listed here for completeness only.

modules.title: MapWindow (the tkinter mini-map)
modules.tagline: A tkinter window that polls every 100 ms and redraws the mini-map without stealing focus
modules.summary: MapWindow polls a source (LiveSource or ReplaySource) every 100 ms, folds the records into a State, and shows `MapView.draw(state)` as a Tk PhotoImage. Live, it is shown without ever being activated, so the game keeps the keyboard focus and stays on top for screen captures; a replay is an ordinary window with keys to pause, change speed and jump.
modules.details_md:
**Why focus matters.** The key player only presses keys while the game is the foreground window, and screen
captures see whatever window is on top. So a live window must never take the focus or cover the game.

**Showing it without activating it (live).**
- `root.withdraw()` first: showing a Tk window the usual way would activate it.
- After `update_idletasks()`, the real frame handle comes from `root.wm_frame()`; `_no_activate` ORs
  `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` (0x08000000) into its extended style (`GWL_EXSTYLE`, -20), so clicks no longer activate it.
- `_show_inactive` calls `ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE)` and, only when a position was given (the command line
  placed it beside the game, never over it), `SetWindowPos(HWND_TOPMOST, ..., SWP_NOMOVE | SWP_NOSIZE | SWP_NOACTIVATE)`
  to keep it above other windows while still inactive.
- If the foreground window changed anyway, `_hand_focus_back` calls `SetForegroundWindow` on the window that had it.
- The position comes from `gamelab/__main__.py`'s `_beside_game` (right of the game's client area, else left, else
  below, on a monitor); with no room it is `None`, the window manager places it and it is not kept on top.

**Replay mode** (`--replay` or `--plan`): no focus tricks; key bindings toggle `source.paused` (space), double or halve
`source.speed` (`+`/`-`), and jump 10 s (`Right`/`Left`) through `_seek`, which rebuilds a fresh State from every
record up to the new position (`ReplaySource.seek`).

**The loop.** `run()` schedules `_tick` with `root.after(POLL_MS)`. Each tick: `source.poll()` gives `(fresh, records)`;
`fresh` (a newer run started) replaces the State; records are applied; if the state's map differs from the view's
model id, `view_for(map)` gives the right `MapView`; the picture is redrawn only if something came.

**Getting pixels into Tk** without Pillow: `ppm()` writes the RGB array as a binary PPM (`P6 w h 255` header + bytes),
which `tk.PhotoImage(data=..., format="PPM")` reads. The PhotoImage is kept on `self._photo`, because Tk shows a blank
picture once its PhotoImage is garbage collected.

modules.title: State (the run as the mini-map sees it)
modules.tagline: Folds telemetry records into the latest record per topic, her trail and log lines
modules.summary: A dataclass holding what the mini-map draws: the latest record of each kept topic, the tour merged across records, her last 240 positions and the last 9 log lines. `apply(record)` folds one telemetry record in; `her()` gives her current position. The web page carries a JavaScript copy of the same rules.
modules.details_md:
Telemetry records are plain dicts `{"t": seconds, "topic": ..., **data}` (`gamelab/telemetry.py`). `State.apply`
handles them by topic:

| Topic | What `apply` does |
|---|---|
| `route` (the planned moves to a platform), `chain` (the moves being carried out in one key plan), `monsters` (as the planner predicts them), `stance` (the fight's last decision), `drops` (remembered for later), `hunt` (the hunt loop's rule and objective), `exp`, `memory` (the monsters she remembers): the `LATEST` topics | the record replaces the field of that name |
| `session` | kept whole; its `map` (if present) sets `State.map`, which picks the map view |
| `scene` | kept whole (her, HP, MP, monsters, loot, players); her `(x, y)` appended to the trail |
| `glance` | the navigator's quick position checks while a chain runs: `(x, y)` appended to the trail |
| `tour` | merged into the previous tour dict (the sweep's `order`, `safe`, `grounds` first, then each `stop` and `spot`) |
| `trip` | arrived or gave up: `route` and `chain` cleared |
| `event`, `log` | their `text` (or an event's `kind`) appended to the log lines |

Every record's `t` becomes `State.t`, the run's clock as far as the picture knows. Any other topic (for example
`tracks`, `attack`, `moved`, `gc`, `perf`) is ignored.

`her()` returns the last scene's `her` dict with its `x, y` replaced by the newest trail point, so a glance between two
looks moves her without waiting for the next scene. It returns `None` while she hasn't been placed (no scene, or
`her.x` is `None`).

The trail and log are `deque`s with `maxlen` (`TRAIL` = 240, `LOG_LINES` = 9), so old entries fall off on their own.
The web server keeps its own longer log (`web.LOG_KEEP` = 40) beside the State, and its page receives `LATEST` and
`TRAIL` written into its JavaScript so the browser's copy of `apply` keeps exactly what this one keeps.

modules.title: MapView (pure drawing)
modules.tagline: State in, RGB picture out: the map and every layer the stack sees and plans
modules.summary: MapView fits a map from the game data into a picture of a given width and draws a State on it with OpenCV: platforms, ropes and portals, the tour, predicted monsters, the planned route and running chain, drops, her attack reach, remembered and seen monsters, other players, her trail and her, plus a text panel. It is pure (no window, no I/O), so it is tested offline; it also provides the colours the web page uses and the coverage report's picture.
modules.details_md:
**Fitting the map.** From the `MapModel` (`gamelab/localization/mapdata.py`): x bounds are the platforms' ends
and the ropes, padded 30 map units each side; y bounds are platform tops, each segment's start height (`y1`) and rope ends, padded 110 above
and 30 below. `scale = (width - 2 * margin) / (x1 - x0)`; the map is `map_h` px tall and the
text panel (`panel`, 170 px by default) sits under it. `pt(x, y)` converts map units to picture px.

**Caching.** `_draw_base` draws walls, ropes, platforms (with their id) and portals once per view. `_roles_layer` keeps a
copy with the tour's safe platforms (teal, `SAFE`) and hunting grounds (bright green, `GROUND`) drawn in, redrawn
only when those lists change: drawn every time they were a quarter of a 900-px picture's 3.6 ms.

**Layers** (`_layers`, in drawing order): the tour's stops numbered in order (current one filled, `HER` yellow) and the
diamond of the spot she shoots from; the planner's monster predictions (red bars over each monster's reach on its
platform); the planned route (cyan: parabolic `_arc`s for `jump`, `walk_off` and `hop`, arrows otherwise, a dot at the
first move's start); the running chain (magenta spans 6 units above the platform and a dot where each leg ends);
remembered drops (hollow squares); the hunt loop's piles (hers bright, others dim, expected ones small, urgent ones red);
her attack reach; remembered monsters; monsters in the last look (and the sweep's `swept`), coloured by `KIND`, ringed
red when the last throw aimed at them, with a green HP bar when the look saw one (`bar`, shown once a monster is hit); loot on the ground; other players by kind
(`PLAYERS`); her trail; and her (a yellow dot, an arrow for her facing, a magenta ring when her name tag was hidden and
she was placed from her minimap dot).

**Her reach** (`_reach`): a band each side from `y - SHOT_UP` to `y + SHOT_DOWN` (60 units each), from `shot_dx(0)`
to `STAR_REACH` (434) out, cut short by `attack.reach.clear_span` at a wall of her platform's foothold group; the side
she faces brighter. It is alpha-blended (`REACH_ALPHA` 0.35) into only the rows the bands cover, as one block of whole
rows plus one, so the result stays pixel-identical: blending each band's own rectangle left a px one level off in 4 of
435 pictures (OpenCV's vector code blends all but a block's last few px).

**Remembered monsters** (`_monsters_remembered`): a ring of the kind's colour faded by `remembered_alpha(age)` = max(0.25,
1 - age / 20 s), the age counted on to the state's time; broken (six arcs) once looks covering the place have missed
it; a cross for one killed (red) or forgotten (dim).

**Crop.** `draw(state, crop=(left, top, w, h))` draws just that part of the map (used by the web server's "around her"
JPEG): a shallow copy of the view with its origin moved. On a 2250-px map, cutting 900 px went from 11 ms to 1.5-2 ms.
It differs from cutting the full picture only where OpenCV antialiases lines cut at the edges: 11-27 px of 648,000 on
five recorded runs.

**Text panel** (`_panel`): HP and MP bars, the mode, the clock, her x and platform and how she was placed, other
players, her EXP and EXP a minute; then the fight's last decision, the chain's text, the hunt loop's rule, objective and
EXP/s here against the rate to beat; then as many log lines as fit (cut to 110 chars).

**Shared with the web page.** `STYLE`, `KIND`, `PLAYERS`, `JUMP_ARC`, `REACH_ALPHA`, `REMEMBER_FADE_S` and
`REMEMBER_FAINT` are sent in `/map.json`, so the browser's renderer uses the same colours and numbers.

**Coverage picture.** `coverage_picture(model, rows)` draws every route move by what runs did with it (taken green, thicker
the more often; planned but never taken yellow; never planned red), with a legend: used by
`python -m gamelab coverage` through `analysis/coverage.py`'s rows.

modules.title: Sources (live, replay, a planned route)
modules.tagline: Where the mini-map's records come from: followed live, replayed, or planned offline
modules.summary: Every source answers `poll() -> (fresh, records)`. LiveSource follows the newest run's telemetry file as it grows, merging what's on screen from the perception service's file with the hunting command's plans; ReplaySource plays a recorded run at its own pace with pause, speed and seek; `load` reads a recording and `planned` makes a still picture of a route planned offline.
modules.details_md:
**The source protocol.** `poll()` returns `(fresh, records)`: `fresh` is True when a different run started
(the window and the page start their State over); `records` are the new telemetry dicts since the last poll.

**_Followed: one kind of file, followed.** It keeps a `telemetry.Follower` (reads what was appended since the last
call, holding back a half-written last line) on the newest file matching its `match`. The folder is rescanned at most
every `rescan_s` (1 s) through `telemetry.newest`, which goes by each file's last write. When the newest file changes:
- if its first record is a `session` record whose `continues` names the file being followed, it is the run's next part
  (a run goes on in a new file past 64 MB): the rest of the old file is read, then the new one, and `fresh` stays False;
- if the new file is still empty (a part is made a moment before its first line), the next scan sees it;
- otherwise it is a new run: `fresh` is True.

**LiveSource: two files merged.** Hunting commands write `<time>-<command>.jsonl`; the perception service (which looks at
every frame, always) writes `<time>-perceive.jsonl` (`perceive_file`). LiveSource follows both:
- No command file yet: the service's file is the run.
- A command file appears: it becomes the run, from its start (`fresh`).
- While the service's file has given records within `PERCEIVE_LIVE_S` (3 s): the screen's topics come from it
  (`PERCEIVED`: `scene`, `tracks`, `exp`, plus the events in `PERCEIVED_EVENTS`: `died`, `exp_gain`, `hp_drop`,
  `touch`, `touch_fix`), the command's own scenes are left out, and the rest (routes, chains, the hunt's rules, the
  log) comes from the command. The service's scenes don't know which way she faces, so the `HER_OWN` fields
  (`facing`, `facing_by`, `facing_keys`, `facing_seen`, `facing_strong`) from the command's latest scene are copied onto
  them. The merged list is sorted by `t`.
- Otherwise the command's records alone.

The command files are scanned with `recent_s = COMMANDS_RECENT_S` (1 day) and the service's with telemetry's
`RECENT_S` (7 days): `telemetry.newest` asks `os.stat` of every file the directory says was written within that time,
because on NTFS the directory's copy of a still-open file's last write is stale. On the live folder (340 files, 20
written within a day, 2026-10-26) a scan took 1.5 ms of CPU against 14.3 ms with 7 days.

**ReplaySource.** Records sorted by `t`; `pos` (s into the recording) advances by elapsed wall time times `speed` unless
`paused`; `poll` releases every record with `t - t0 <= pos`. `seek(seconds)` moves `pos` (never below 0) and returns
every record up to it, so the caller rebuilds its State. Never `fresh`.

**load(path)**: a `.jsonl` telemetry file through `telemetry.read`; anything else is an older sweep track (JSON with
`track: [[t, x, y, platform], ...]`) turned into one `session` record and a `scene` per position.

**planned(model, src, x, dst)**: what `--plan SRC DST` shows, no game needed: `motion.route.Planner(model).plan(src, x,
dst)` gives the moves (`route_record`), `motion.flow.Flow(model, names).chain(...)` the first key plan's legs
(`chain_record`), with dummy key names since nothing is sent; plus a `session` (mode `plan`), a `scene` placing her,
and a log line listing the moves.

modules.title: The web page server (Feed, SSE stream, page)
modules.tagline: The mini-map for a phone: records pushed over Server-Sent Events, drawn on a canvas
modules.summary: A standard-library HTTP server that follows the same sources as the window, keeps the State in a Feed updated by a thread every 25 ms, and pushes a snapshot then each batch of records to every open page over Server-Sent Events. The page draws the map itself on a canvas with the window's colours from /map.json. It also routes /review (recordings) and /tls (decrypted captures), and is what the Cloudflare tunnel serves.
modules.details_md:
`python -m gamelab minimap` starts this server and the window in one process (`--web-only` or `python -m
gamelab web`: the page only, `--window-only`: no page); default `--host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765`. Standard library only:
`ThreadingHTTPServer` with HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, Nagle off, a 30 s handler timeout.

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `/` | the page (`PAGE`, with URLs and State constants written in) |
| `/events` | the Server-Sent Events stream: a snapshot, then updates, pings |
| `/map.json` | the map geometry, view bounds, colours and reach (`map_payload`) |
| `/control` (POST) | replay only: `action=pause|faster|slower|back|on` |
| `/frame.jpg`, `/state.json`, `/clock.json` | the map as JPEG (`?view=her`), the text, the run's clock; the page doesn't need them (tests, a quick look, the no-JavaScript image, `?debug=1`'s round trip) |
| `/review...` | `ui.review` |
| `/tls...` | `ui.tls` (Cloudflare Access-checked) |

**The Feed** holds the State. Its `telemetry` thread calls `step()` every `POLL_S` (25 ms): `source.poll()`, then under
the lock either `_restart` (a new run: fresh State, ring cleared, `epoch` + 1) or `_apply` (fold, append each record
to `ring` with a rising `seq`, `version` + 1). Both `notify_all` on a Condition the streams wait on. Live, `_timed`
notes the newest record's `t`: within 5 s of this computer's clock, the run is on this computer; otherwise (a simulated
run, which stamps the simulator's own clock) the page's clock is the newest record's `t` moved on at the pace records
arrive, measured every 2 s and clamped to 0-64.

**A stream.** Each `/events` connection gets its own handler thread and a `Cursor`. `Feed.updates(cursor, 5 s)` waits on
the Condition and returns:
- `snapshot` when the cursor's epoch is old or it fell behind the ring (4096 records): the session, the tour, the latest
  of each `LATEST` topic, the scene, her trail, the log lines and the text;
- `update` with the records since the cursor, `_coalesce`d (of the `LATEST` topics only the last one stays; every
  position and log line is kept, so the page's State ends up the same), and what changed in the text, at most every
  `STATUS_EVERY_S` (0.2 s);
- `ping` after 5 s with nothing to send. Snapshots, updates and pings all carry `now` and `rate`, the run's clock.
`_event` writes `id: <seq>` for updates and `event: <name>` for the others, in one write each. Past `MAX_STREAMS` (16)
the oldest is ended `crowded`: it gets a `crowded` event and its page stops rather than reconnect and crowd out the next.

**The page** (`PAGE`, about 600 lines of HTML, CSS and JavaScript) keeps a copy of `State.apply`, opens an `EventSource`,
and draws on a canvas at the device's pixel ratio, layer for layer as `MapView.draw`, with `/map.json`'s colours.
Her position is drawn `DELAY` (0.1 s of the run) behind the run's clock and interpolated (`herAt`) between trail points
less than `GAP` (0.6 s) apart; it redraws only when something moved. "Around her" (the default under 700 px wide) is
`ZOOM` (2.5) times bigger, `AROUND` (0.8) of the width tall, with an eased camera. A stream quiet for 12.5 s is reopened
(iOS Safari can leave one dead behind a locked screen), and one quiet over 6 s when the page is shown again. Text,
log and clock refresh 4 times a second; replay buttons POST to `/control`. On a desktop-width page opened on
127.0.0.1 it shows the LAN address and a QR code (qrcodejs from cdnjs). `?debug=1` adds a corner with fps, draw time,
KB/s, reconnects and lateness; `?delay=0` draws the newest position.

**Why push and draw on the phone** (the module docstring): the page used to fetch the text every 400 ms and a 40 KB JPEG:
1.6 pictures a second, 280 ms old on average (540 at worst), 43% of her positions, 45-70 KB/s. Pushed, a record reaches
the page in about 20 ms for about 2 KB/s.

**Exposure.** It asks for no key or password: whoever reaches the address (the LAN, or the Cloudflare tunnel's hostname)
can watch and steer a replay. It only reads telemetry and never sends keys. `/tls/` is the one path that requires a
Cloudflare Access login for requests that came through the tunnel.

modules.title: Review pages (/review)
modules.tagline: Overlaid recordings served frame by frame to a phone, with smaller frames and video
modules.summary: Serves folders of overlaid frames (perception's outcome drawn on each frame of a recording) under /review: a listing of sets and groups, a mobile viewer that steps and plays frames, meta.json, the frames (optionally re-encoded smaller), the set's files with byte ranges, and the set as a downloadable MP4. The sets are made elsewhere (the overlay tool, and tools/review_pages for the Lie Detector and Violetta).
modules.details_md:
**Where sets live.** `ROOT` is `GAMELAB_REVIEW_ROOT`, else `MapleHelper-scratch/golden-tree` beside the repo.
A *set* is a folder with a `frames/` folder of `00000.jpg ...`; it may also hold `legend.png`, `overlay.mp4`,
`README.md`, `LEGEND.md` and `problems.json` (`[{"frames": [a, b], "what": "..."}]`, the frames worth a look). A
*group* is a folder with no `frames/` of its own and sets inside (one level only).

**Routes** (`handle`, called from `web._Handler.do_GET`):
- `/review`: the groups and sets; `/review/<group>/`: a group's sets;
- `/review/[<group>/]<set>/`: the viewer (`_VIEWER`);
- `.../meta.json`: `meta()` — frame count, last frame number, problems, files present, frame rate and version;
- `.../frames/N.jpg[?w=W&q=Q]`: a frame, as it is or made smaller (`smaller`);
- `.../legend.png`, `overlay.mp4`, `README.md`, `LEGEND.md`: sent by `_file` with byte ranges;
- `.../video.mp4`: `video_of()` sent as an attachment.
Names must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` and frames `\d{5}.jpg`, so nothing outside a set is served.

**Smaller frames.** `w` clamped to 64-4096 and `q` to 30-95; never wider than the frame (INTER_AREA resize), quality 85
when only `w` is given. Kept in an in-memory LRU of 96 MB (`SMALL_CACHE`), keyed by path, mtime, size, width and
quality; sent with `Cache-Control: max-age=86400`. A 750 px frame of 178 KB is about 40 KB at 540 px. JPEG, not WebP:
WebP took 40-100 ms a frame against 1-4 ms for 10-25% less (commit 9a51e6f4).

**Version.** `version()` is the newest frame mtime in ms, hex; the viewer puts it in each frame URL (`&v=`) so a set
drawn again is fetched again instead of read from the day-long browser cache.

**Frame rate.** `fps()`: the `overlay.mp4`'s rate (0-120), else the `NNfps` in the set's name, else 15.

**The viewer** (inline HTML/JS): back/on by 1 and 15, play at 2, 5, 15 fps or the recorded rate (added and marked
"(recorded)"), a slider, a frame number box, swipe (over 50 px) and arrow keys, full size with scrolling, a data saver
(on by default, remembered: frames as wide as shown, at most 1.5 device px per CSS px, in 60 px steps, quality 60),
problem buttons, links to the set's files, the frame in the URL `#`. It preloads from the start: the frames nearest
ahead of the one shown, then just behind, 8 at a time, up to 600 ahead and 60 behind ("loading n/N"). No double-tap
zoom (`touch-action: manipulation`).

**Video.** `video_of`: the set's `overlay.mp4` if any; else one made from its frames by `ui.video.frames_video` at its
frame rate, kept in `ROOT/.videos/<set>-<version>.mp4` (`<group>__<set>-...` for a set in a group) (written as `.making.mp4` then renamed; older versions
deleted); one making at a time per set (a lock per set name), others wait.

**Byte ranges** (`_file`): `Range: bytes=a-b`, `a-` and `-N` (the last N bytes); 416 when unsatisfiable; 206 with
`Content-Range`; written in 1 MB chunks. Phones' video players ask this way.

modules.tagline: Frames to a phone-playable H.264 MP4 using Windows' own encoder, index first
modules.summary: Turns a review set's frames into an MP4 a phone can play: frames into a temporary MJPEG AVI with OpenCV, re-encoded to H.264 by Windows Media Foundation through h264.ps1, then the MP4 index (moov) moved before the media (faststart). modules.details_md:
**Why this detour.** An iPhone plays no MPEG-4 Part 2, which is all OpenCV writes here ('mp4v'); OpenCV's
FFmpeg has no H.264 encoder on this machine (it asks for OpenH264's DLL). Windows 10 ships an H.264 encoder, reachable
from PowerShell through WinRT's `MediaTranscoder`, with nothing downloaded or installed.

**frames_video(frames, fps, dst)**:
1. Reads the first frame for the size; the output is padded to even width and height (H.264 takes even sizes only:
   a black column or row via `copyMakeBorder`). Frames of another size are resized to the first's; unreadable ones
   become black.
2. Writes the frames to `dst` with its suffix swapped for `.mjpg.avi` (fourcc `MJPG`, at `fps`).
3. `h264()` runs `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File h264.ps1 -In ... -Out <dst stem>.h264.mp4 -Width W
   -Height H -Fps round(fps) -Bitrate 8*W*H` with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and a 600 s timeout; success means exit 0 and a
   non-empty output.
4. On success `faststart(raw, dst)` and returns `"h264"`; otherwise `mp4v(avi, dst, fps)` re-writes the AVI as OpenCV's
   MPEG-4 Part 2 and returns `"mp4v"`.
5. The temporary AVI and raw MP4 are always deleted.

**faststart(src, dst)**: walks the top-level MP4 boxes (`_boxes`, handling 64-bit sizes and size 0 = to the end). If
`moov` is already before `mdat` it copies the file. Otherwise it takes `moov` out, adds its size to every chunk offset
inside it (`_shift` recurses through the container boxes in `CONTAINERS` and rewrites `stco` 32-bit and `co64` 64-bit
offsets; an `stco` offset past 4 GB raises), and writes ftyp, moov, then the rest, via a `.tmp` file renamed into
place. This is what ffmpeg's `-movflags +faststart` does, so a phone can start playing as the file arrives.

modules.tagline: PowerShell: re-encode a video to H.264 MP4 with WinRT's MediaTranscoder
modules.summary: A PowerShell script that loads WinRT types and re-encodes any video Media Foundation reads into an H.264 MP4 of a given size, frame rate and bitrate, with no audio. Called by `ui/video.py`'s `h264()`; uses only Windows 10's built-in codecs.

Parameters: `-In` and `-Out` (required), `-Width` (default 1696), `-Height` (1030), `-Fps` (15), `-Bitrate`
(12000000). `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`.

Steps:
1. `Add-Type System.Runtime.WindowsRuntime` and reference the WinRT types `StorageFile`, `MediaTranscoder` and

2. `Await($op, $type)`: finds the generic `AsTask` overload on `System.WindowsRuntimeSystemExtensions` by reflection,

5. A `MediaTranscoder` with `HardwareAccelerationEnabled = $false`; `PrepareFileTranscodeAsync(src, dst, profile)`; if it
   can't transcode, prints `cannot transcode: <reason>` and exits 2; else runs `TranscodeAsync()` and prints
   `h264: <path>`.

`python tools/review_pages/build.py {ld,violetta} [clip keys ...] [--missing] [--list] [--root DIR] [--force]
[--weights FILE]`. A clip's key is the first 15 characters of its folder name (its stamp, `20261104-180343`).

**Clips and groups.** Clips are folders in `gamelab/lab/alarm_clips` (`paths.ALARM_CLIPS`) matching `FORMS`:
`*mini-game-notice*` for `ld`, `*countdown*` for `violetta`. Each form has page groups (`GROUPS`): `ld-reference`,
`ld-outline-pf3`, `ld-speed-compare`; and `violetta`, `violetta-yolo`. A clip's page in a group is
`<root>/<group>/<key>-<fps>fps/` (`pages`).

**Planning.** `--list` prints, per group, the clips with no page and builds nothing. Otherwise `plan()` decides per clip
which groups to build, printing why it skips: an approved clip's `ld-reference` is never rebuilt; an existing page is
skipped unless `--force`. With `--force`, `clear()` deletes the pages about to be rebuilt first (the builders never write
over one). For `ld`, a clip with no worked-out range (`lib.clip(k)` is `None`) is dropped, having said why.

**build_ld.** First, in the main process, each clip's frames (`lib.load_clip`) and board scrolls (`scrolls`) are made,
because parallel workers would each make them and read each other's half-written files. Clips needing a reference (not
approved, and either the reference page is wanted or no reference file exists) get `reference.one` run for every seed
(`reference.SEEDS` = 0, 1, 2: three runs, their median is the reference) in a `ProcessPoolExecutor(WORKERS=4)`; once all seeds of a clip are back, `reference.build` writes it (and its page if
asked). Then `review_pf3.render(k, "ld-outline-pf3", PF3)` and `review_compare.render(k)`.

**build_violetta.** Runs in `<work>/violetta` (the scripts use relative folders): per clip, a first pass `track2.py` from
14 s after the alarm to a second after the countdown's last sighting (checked on every third frame with
`LieDetectorSpotter.near`), then `solve.main` into `solved/`, `track5.py` sprite matches into `dets5/`; YOLO
(`yolo_detect.py` with the weights) into `detsY.part/` then moved into `detsY/`; the rules solver's tally
(`rules.py`) for each detector; then `build_review.py` for each group. Each step is skipped when its output exists;
the trackers and YOLO write under a `.part` name first and rename when done, so a crash leaves no half file taken for
done.

modules.tagline: Captures decrypted in memory and shaped for the page: connections, requests, bodies
modules.summary: Finds the .pcap captures under the root with their key logs, decrypts one in a background thread when the page opens it (a few seconds for 90 MB, nothing written), and turns it into connections and items: HTTP/1.x exchanges, HTTP/2 streams (HPACK decoded here) and WebSocket messages, with bodies decoded (gzip, deflate, zstd, NGS CE: G responses, NGS AE: G requests, brotli if installed). Keeps the 4 most recently used.
modules.details_md:
`discover` finds every `.pcap` up to 4 folders down (skipping the recorder's own `tls`, `streams`, `bodies` and `replay` output folders), with the `keys*.log` / `sslkeys*.log` / `*.keylog` files beside it as its key logs.
`Library.open(cid, local)` returns the `Capture` for a capture id (a hash of its path) and frame-trust setting,
starting a `tls-decrypt` daemon thread on first open; it keeps the 4 most recently used in memory. `Capture.stale()` says
when its pcap or key logs changed since (a recording still going), so the page can offer Reload. `Capture._run` calls `decrypt.frame_sources`, `load_keylogs` and `decrypt_conn` for every TCP connection, reporting progress every 25 connections, and builds the summary the page shows (connections, decrypted, records, lost bytes, hosts, seconds taken, whether the NGS decoder and brotli are there). A capture under a
folder named `local` (the parent of the pcap's own folder) is taken as captured on this PC unless the page says
otherwise.

modules.title: TLS viewer front end (JavaScript)
modules.tagline: The /tls/ page's script: capture picker, request and connection lists, details, x-csauth
modules.summary: Plain JavaScript for the TLS viewer: lists captures, opens one through the API and polls until it is decrypted, shows the Requests, Connections and x-csauth tabs with filters, and a detail pane (headers, bodies as JSON tree, text or hex, TLS records). Captured data is only ever put into the page as text nodes.
modules.details_md: All captured bytes go through `el()`, which builds elements with text nodes, never HTML. `openCap` asks `api/open` every 250 ms until the capture is `ready` (showing its progress), then loads `api/summary`; `checkStale` asks every 10 s whether the capture's files changed and lights the Reload button. State lives in one object `S`; the selected capture and view are kept in the URL hash; the list width in localStorage. Its header comment still says it is served by `.tools/tls_web.py` (its origin); here `gamelab/ui/tls/__init__.py` serves it.

flows.title: How a record reaches a phone
flows.summary: From a telemetry record to her dot moving on the phone's canvas: about 20 ms once the line is in the file (measured 2026-10-20), plus up to 0.2 s waiting for the recorder's next batched write.
flows.trigger: A hunting command or the perception service emits a telemetry record while the web page is open.

steps.text: The recorder's own thread appends the record as one JSON line, in batches FLUSH_S (0.2 s) apart at most.
The Feed's `telemetry` thread wakes every 25 ms and polls its source.

Reads what was appended to the command's and the service's files; while the service's file is live (records within 3 s) the screen's topics come from it and the merged list is sorted by t, otherwise the command's records come alone.
Under the lock: each record folded into the State and appended to the ring with the next seq; version + 1; every waiting stream notified.
Each stream's thread wakes, takes the records after its cursor, coalesces superseded LATEST records, adds text changes if 0.2 s have passed.
Writes one SSE message (`id: seq`, `data: JSON`) in one write, Nagle off, so it goes out at once.
In the browser: the page sets its clock from now/rate and applies each record to its copy of the State.
On the next animation frame the canvas is redrawn if anything moved, her position interpolated 100 ms behind the run's clock.

flows.title: One tick of the mini-map window
flows.summary: How the tkinter window refreshes its picture.

steps.text: Polls the source for (fresh, records).
A fresh run starts a new State; each record is folded in.
If the State's map changed, `view_for(map)` gives that map's MapView (made once per map).
The cached base with the tour's platforms, then every layer and the text panel, as an RGB array.
The array becomes PPM bytes, a Tk PhotoImage kept on the window, shown in its label.

flows.title: A replay jumped back from the phone
flows.summary: Every open page restarts from a snapshot when a replay jumps.
flows.trigger: The page's "« 10 s" button while `minimap --replay FILE` (or `web --replay`) runs.

steps.text: POST /control?action=back: the body (if any) is read, the action passed to the Feed; 200 or 400.
Under the lock, calls the source's seek with -SEEK_S.
Moves the position back 10 s and returns every record up to it.
A new State built from those records, the ring cleared, epoch + 1, streams notified.
Each stream sees its epoch is old and sends a snapshot.
In the browser: the page rebuilds its State from the snapshot and resets its clock and camera.

flows.title: Downloading a review set as a video
flows.summary: The viewer's Download video button, for a set with only frames.

steps.text: Checks the set name and routes video.mp4.
No overlay.mp4: looks for ROOT/.videos/<set>-<version>.mp4; if missing, takes the set's lock and makes it.
Writes the frames into a temporary MJPEG AVI at the set's frame rate, padded to even sizes.

Runs h264.ps1 in PowerShell: Windows' MediaTranscoder re-encodes to H.264 at 8 bits a pixel a second. If it fails, `mp4v` re-writes the AVI as OpenCV's MPEG-4 Part 2 instead and the next step is skipped.
Moves moov before mdat and shifts the chunk offsets, so a phone plays it as it arrives.
Renames the finished `.making.mp4` to `<set>-<version>.mp4` and deletes the set's older versions; then releases the set's lock.
Sends the MP4 as an attachment, whole or by byte range.
